data.title: Individual Investors Bought Nearly $2 Billion in Nvidia Shares This Week — WSJ
data.description:
By Vicky Ge Huang

A tumultuous week for Nvidia has triggered a wave of dip-buying by individual investors.

They have wasted little time scooping up shares of the AI chipmaker after the resignation of CEO Jensen Huang.

Through mid-Friday afternoon, they had snapped up $1.96 billion worth of Nvidia shares this week, the biggest week of retail buying in the stock since March 2025, when they bought $1.99 billion of the shares, according to data from flow-tracking firm Vanda Research.

"With the final stretch of the session still to go, and assuming only modest further buying, there is a good chance we break through the $2 billion level this week," said Viraj Patel, global macro strategist at Vanda Research.

This item is part of a Wall Street Journal live coverage event. The full stream can be found by searching P/WSJL (WSJ Live Coverage).

data.title: CIBL, Inc. Reports Third Quarter 2026 Results
data.description:
CIBL, Inc. (“CIBL” or the “Company”; OTC Pink ®: CIBY), announced third quarter 2026 financial and operating results.

Third Quarter 2026 Highlights

  • Revenues decreased 3.8% to $536,000 in the third quarter of 2026 from $557,000 in the third quarter of 2025

  • EBITDA from operations decreased 6.7% to $140,000 from $150,000

  • Net loss was $25,000 in the third quarter of 2026 compared to net income of $86,000 in the third quarter of 2025

  • Loss per share was $2.30 in the third quarter of 2026 compared to income per share of $7.46 in the third quarter of 2025

  • Cash and investments were $19.0 million or $1,756 per share as of September 30, 2026

  • CIBL repurchased 13 of its common shares at an average price of $1,715 per share in the third quarter of 2026

Nine Months Ending September 30, 2026 Highlights

  • Revenues increased 16.7% to $1,880,000 for the nine months ending September 30, 2026 from $1,611,000 for the nine months ending September 30, 2025

  • EBITDA from operations increased 33.3% to $524,000 from $393,000

  • Net income was $65,000 for the nine months ending September 30, 2026 compared to $215,000 for the nine months ending September 30, 2025

  • Earnings per share were $5.96 per share for the nine months ending September 30, 2026 compared to $18.45 for the nine months ending September 30, 2025

  • CIBL repurchased 407 of its common shares at an average price of $1,713 per share for the nine months ending September 30, 2026

Results from Operations

Three Months Ended September 30, 2026

Revenues decreased 3.8% to $536,000 in the third quarter of 2026 from $557,000 in the third quarter of 2025 due to lower service revenues primarily due to installation activity in 2025 partially offset by growth in CLEC services.

EBITDA from operations decreased 6.7% to $140,000 for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026 from $150,000 for the third quarter ended September 30, 2025 due to the decrease in revenues discussed above partially offset by a one-time non-regulated expense credit.

Other income decreased $75,000 to $200,000 for the third quarter ending September 30, 2026 from $275,000 for the third quarter ending September 30, 2025. The decrease was primarily due to deceases in the Company’s equity in earnings of affiliated companies and lower yields on U.S. Treasuries.

Nine Months Ended September 30, 2026

Revenues increased 16.7% to $1,880,000 for the nine months ending September 30, 2026 from $1,611,000 for the nine months ending September 30, 2025 due to increased service revenues primarily due to installation activity in 2026.

EBITDA from operations increased 33.3% to $524,000 for the nine months ending September 30, 2026 from $393,000 for the nine months ending September 30, 2025 due to the increase in revenues discussed above partially offset by less capitalized labor for plant under construction and switch replacements.

Other income decreased $265,000 to $539,000 for the nine months ending September 30, 2026 from $804,000 for the nine months ending September 30, 2025. The decrease was primarily due to deceases in the Company’s equity in earnings of affiliated companies and lower yields on U.S. Treasuries.

Other Highlights

Capital expenditures were $68,000 and $76,000 for the nine months ending September 30, 2026, and 2025, respectively.

On September 24, 2025, CIBL acquired 100,000 shares of The Gabelli Global Small and Mid Cap Value Trust Series E Cumulative Preferred Shares (“Preferred Shares”) at a cost of $10 per share. These Preferred Shares included a dividend of 5.2% per annum payable semiannually (March and September) with mandatory and optional redemptions by the issuer on September 26, 2027, and September 27, 2026, respectively. These Preferred Shares include an optional put by the Company on March 26, 2026, September 26, 2026, and March 26, 2027. As of December 31, 2025, these Preferred Shares are included in other investments with an aggregate fair value of $1,000,000.

Through September 30, 2026, the Company acquired 407 of its shares at an average price of $1,713 per share. As of September 30, 2026, CIBL has 10,837 shares outstanding. Since its spin-off from LICT Corporation in 2007, CIBL has repurchased 16,029 of its shares for $22.9 million, or an average price of $1,433 per share. As of September 30, 2026, there were 567 shares remaining to be purchased under the Company’s share repurchase program.

CIBL’s Board of Directors continues to evaluate a broad range of strategic alternatives for the company to create shareholder value.

About CIBL, Inc.

CIBL is a holding company with interests in broadband operations. CIBL’s operations consist of Bretton Woods Telephone Company and World Surfer, Inc. and Brick Skirt, providers of broadband and communication services in Northern New Hampshire and Western New York State, respectively. CIBL is listed on OTC Pink® under the symbol CIBY, and information can be obtained on our website: www.ciblinc.com.

data.title: CIBL, Inc. (CIBY) Q3 Revenue Fell 3.8% to $536K
data.description:
CIBL's Q3 2026 revenue fell 3.8% to $536K from $557K a year earlier, and operating EBITDA fell 6.7% to $140K from $150K. Nine-month revenue rose 16.7% to $1.9M from $1.6M, while EBITDA rose 33.3% to $524K from $393K.

Material Details

#DetailAI Analyst View
1Q3 revenue fell 3.8% to $536KYear-over-year decline points to softer quarterly activity; the release attributes it mainly to lower service revenue after 2025 installation work.
2Q3 operating EBITDA fell 6.7% to $140KOperating earnings declined from $150K a year earlier, despite a one-time non-regulated expense credit.
3Nine-month revenue rose 16.7% to $1.9MGrowth from $1.6M was primarily driven by installation activity in 2026, which may not indicate recurring growth.
4Nine-month operating EBITDA rose 33.3% to $524KEBITDA improved from $393K, though the release cites installation-related revenue and lower capitalized labor among the drivers.
5Repurchased 407 shares through September 30The company said 567 shares remained under its repurchase program; the release gives no total spend for this period.

Context by AI Analyst

This is a mixed quarterly report: Q3 revenue and operating EBITDA declined, while nine-month results increased largely with installation activity. Further quarters showing revenue and EBITDA growth beyond installation-driven work, or a specific strategic-alternatives update, would make this a larger catalyst.

data.title: Beasley Broadcast Group, Inc. (BBGI) Q3 Revenue Falls 16.1% to $42.8M
data.description:
Third-quarter revenue was $42.8M, down 16.1% year over year, or 10.2% on a same-station basis. Adjusted EBITDA was $1.3M versus $3.9M a year earlier.

Material Details

#DetailAI Analyst View
1Revenue $42.8M, down 16.1% YoYDeclining advertising revenue remains the central operating pressure; same-station revenue fell 10.2%.
2Adjusted EBITDA $1.3M vs. $3.9M a year agoProfitability weakened despite lower costs, underscoring the effect of reduced advertising revenue.
3Digital margin ~32% vs. 21% a year agoHigher margins indicate improving digital efficiency, though same-station digital revenue fell 12.3% in the quarter.
4First-lien notes reduced to ~ $3.6MLower debt supports financial flexibility; the company also reported more than $10M in net proceeds from post-quarter asset sales.

Context by AI Analyst

These results show continued revenue pressure alongside cost reductions and debt restructuring, with digital margins improving despite lower quarterly digital revenue. A sustained recovery in core advertising, stronger cash generation, and further debt reduction would make the turnaround a larger catalyst.
